title: PRAIM: AI finds more breast cancers in German screening
summary: In a prospective study of over 460,000 women at twelve German sites, AI-assisted reading detected 6.7 cancers per thousand exams versus 5.7 without AI. Recall rates for further assessment were 37.4 versus 38.3 per thousand. This observational study does not show a survival benefit, and estimates of workload reduction with automated reading come from simulations.
organization: Universität zu Lübeck; UKSH, and Vara

evidence.tested: A prospective study of over 460,000 women at twelve German sites (2021-2023) compared AI-assisted reading with standard double reading by radiologists: 6.7 vs 5.7 cancers per 1,000 exams.
evidence.unknown: No survival benefit is shown; workload and skipped-review figures come from simulations, and the effect on prognosis is still to be studied.
evidence.ai_role: AI read about half of the mammograms, marking cases as normal or suspicious, with the rest read by double reading.
